items.fact: The campaign has five chapters. PC Gamer counts 91 story missions, while Push Square counts 93, so the totals differ by outlet.

Missions per chapter: Ch.1 has 22, Ch.2 has 11 plus 3 optional, Ch.3 has 26 plus 1 optional, Ch.4 has 25, and Ch.5 has 7. The chapters are centered on the Leonida Keys, Port Gellhorn, Vice City, Vice City again, and Vice City plus Leonida.
Story missions can't be replayed and have no medals. You can make manual saves at the start of each chapter to return to earlier points in the campaign.
The story follows two playable protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Lucia Caminos is introduced in the Prologue, and Jason's allies include Cal, Brian and Donnie.
Chapter 3 is where you can first switch between Jason and Lucia, and it is the longest chapter.
There are 18 collectible card sets. Their sizes range from 12 to 36 cards, for example 24 for the Vice City Flamingos and 36 for Jack of Hearts.
Collecting three cards in each of the five counties unlocks the Collectible Cards achievement. Individual cards can be sold for cash, with rare ones worth thousands.
There are 31 scannable WAiNK Landmarks scattered across Leonida's towns and counties, and they count toward 100% completion.
Magazines and books are collectible. Reading them can unlock phone contacts and fishing spots, and Jason's starting house holds five of them.

Underwater Discoveries are a diving side activity tied to Kenton's Treasures. The shipwreck sites guide shows them in the southern part of Leonida, and you need the Metal Detector, which you get after working for Kenton.

Side activities that stay available after Chapter 1 include the Exotic Animal Front, the two Kingfisher robbery opportunities, and the Bigfoot mission chain. Kenton's shipwrecks and Cal's fishing challenge are only temporarily disabled.
Collectibles are spread across five counties of Leonida. One example is a card found north of Key Lento in South Vice-Dale County.
Robberies are the main income. Loot goes into stash bags and is sold to fences, and most robberies are easier once you can switch between both characters.
Fences pay different prices by specialty. Yasmani in Little Cuba pays well for jewelry and marked bills, and Tyrone pays well for narcotics.
Don't rob banks or loan stores until Chapter 3. Their cash carries dye packs, and you need the Dye Pack Jammer, unlocked in the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check, to avoid them.
You can lose a wanted level by changing your outfit, hiding your weapons or switching vehicles. Dying while carrying stash bags loses both the bags and your cash on hand.
Each chapter moves you to a new safehouse with no way back, so save manually in each chapter if you want to revisit old locations.
The Slim Jim, obtained in the Chapter 2 mission Moses, lets you steal cars quietly. The Chapter 3 Key Cloner phone app is needed for modern keyless cars.
Vans and trucks can hold up to about eight stash bags in the trunk, and motorcycles can't hold any.
Rockstar's first post-launch PS5 update is version 01.002.002. It rolled out in stages, and no official patch notes had been published.

Reported launch issues include a PS5 error code, an Xbox Series X|S glitch that runs gameplay at double speed, and a Chapter 3 soft lock. The soft lock hits players who do a Chapter 2 side mission after Chapter 3 begins, which leaves them stuck as Lucia.
Players have reported crashes and save-system problems. An infinite money glitch worth up to $10,000 per run has been found, and Rockstar may patch it.
